card.name: Verbs of drug interaction effects
card.fires_on: Verbs and linking words in drug-interaction sentences where one drug acts on another, such as 'may reduce', 'can decrease', 'potentiates', and 'Conversely,'. The next word is expected to be an effect on the other drug.

modes.label: Effect verbs
modes.description: A verb saying one drug lowers or raises the effect or exposure of another.
modes.example: Mycophenolate mofetil may<< reduce>> effectiveness of oral contraceptives.

modes.label: Contrast or link words
modes.description: A comma after 'Conversely' or a word like 'on' that introduces the reverse or target of an interaction.
modes.example: potentially resulting in adverse events. Conversely<<,>> adverse effects could result from displacement of par

card.writes: It promotes verb-like word endings such as interpreting, converting and cluded, and suppresses Chinese words meaning 'give to', so it adds little that is clear.
card.plain: It marks the point in a drug-interaction sentence where one drug is said to change the effect of another.
